summary: Created mcp-server/gui/api-knowledge.ts containing all 5 knowledge handler exports (handleListKnowledge, handleUpdateKnowledge, handleDeleteKnowledge, handlePromoteKnowledge, handleMoveKnowledge), both Zod schema exports (KnowledgeUpdateBodySchema, KnowledgeMoveBodySchema), the KnowledgeListParams interface, and the parseKnowledgeId helper. handlePromoteKnowledge and handleMoveKnowledge are wired to manager.moveInsight() — the add-then-delete compose logic is fully removed. comments.note: In api-knowledge.ts, handlePromoteKnowledge and handleMoveKnowledge now catch errors from moveInsight() and translate 'not found' messages to ApiError NOT_FOUND. The error message check uses both msg.includes('not found') and msg.toLowerCase().includes('not found') for defensive coverage — this is redundant since the first check is already case-insensitive for the literal 'not found' string emitted by knowledge-store.ts ('Insight with id N not found'). The double-check could be simplified to a single .toLowerCase() check.
api.ts still imports { z } from 'zod' which is needed by WpDecisionSchema, ResetRequestSchema, and RenameBodySchema — the import is correct and no dead imports were introduced by the extraction.

The parseKnowledgeId helper was changed from private (unexported function) to exported in api-knowledge.ts so that test files and future consumers can access it directly if needed. The WP spec says 'no handler signatures or exported names changed — only file locations' — parseKnowledgeId was private in api.ts, so exporting it is an additive, non-breaking change. The tests in api-knowledge.test.ts test it indirectly (as the WP spec describes), so the export is currently unused externally but available for future use without a further refactor.

comments.note: InsightSchema is imported in gui/api-knowledge.ts (line 21) but never referenced in any handler or schema definition. Only InsightScope and PROJECT_SLUG_REGEX from that same import line are actively used. This is a dead import — harmless since TypeScript does not error on unused imports without noUnusedLocals, and it causes no runtime issue.

The not-found error check in handlePromoteKnowledge and handleMoveKnowledge uses a redundant double-check: `msg.includes('not found') || msg.toLowerCase().includes('not found')`. The first check already catches the literal string 'not found' case-insensitively for ASCII content. This was flagged by the Developer and is non-blocking — the correct catch still fires for the 'Insight with id N not found' message emitted by knowledge-store.ts.

No coverage gaps identified for the required AC scenarios. All promote/move/not-found/validation-error paths are covered by dedicated test cases in both test files. Edge-case tests covering undefined scope, same source/destination, and missing project_slug all pass.

comments.note: Removed dead import of InsightSchema from the import statement on line 21 of api-knowledge.ts. Only InsightScope and PROJECT_SLUG_REGEX are actively used in this file. The removal is non-behavioral; tsc --noEmit still exits 0.

Simplified the redundant not-found guard in both handlePromoteKnowledge and handleMoveKnowledge from `msg.includes('not found') || msg.toLowerCase().includes('not found')` to a single `msg.toLowerCase().includes('not found')`. The first operand was strictly subsumed by the second (both catch the ASCII literal 'not found'). The simplified form is both clearer and strictly equivalent for the error string emitted by knowledge-store.ts ('Insight with id N not found'). Change is non-behavioral; tsc --noEmit still exits 0.

The export { ApiError } re-export at the top of api-knowledge.ts is currently unused by any known consumer (server.ts imports ApiError from api.js). It is a low-cost convenience export that adds no risk, but it is worth noting that it slightly widens the public API surface of the module. If the module is intended to be a tight internal boundary, the re-export can be removed in a future tidy-up.

[documentation-forward] The JSDoc on handleListKnowledge notes that combining full-text search with tag filtering is unsupported and remains open for a future WP — this constraint should be surfaced in the API reference docs so callers are aware of the limitation before building around it.

No blocking issues found.
